data.content_ref: inline:SRC_005 shares mechanism with SRC_004: leaderless synchronization via algorithmic convergence is the precise mechanism by which a decentralized network fails to enforce the global coordination that would break feedback loops. A large service with strictly more internal redundancy inherits an advantage because it can deploy Byzantine fault tolerance or n-version programming to break the same synchronization that the decentralized network cannot. The shared mechanism is refuted if the large service's internal redundancy is homogeneous, so it too cannot break correlation, or if operators have diverse operational goals that break the coupling in the decentralized case.
